candidates.title: Optimal learning of quantum channels in diamond distance
candidates.authors: Antonio Anna Mele, Lennart Bittel
candidates.abstract: Abstract The evolution of quantum states can be described by quantum channels. The task of estimating an unknown quantum channel, known as process tomography, is a central problem in quantum information theory. A long-standing open question is how many uses of an unknown channel are required to learn it to a precision quantified by the standard metric for distinguishing quantum processes, known as the diamond distance. Here we address this by establishing the query complexity of channel tomography with optimal dependence on the dimensions of the input and output spaces and the channel’s Kraus rank at any fixed constant accuracy in diamond distance. We design an algorithm that establishes an upper bound and prove a matching lower bound for learning a channel to the given accuracy. Our algorithm follows the strategy of performing optimal tomography on the Choi-state representation of the process, and we show that channel tomography can be reduced to the well-studied problem of pure-state tomography. As channels subsume states, unitaries and measurements as special cases, our protocol provides a unified framework for tomography of these tasks.

candidates.title: Proximal redox coupling enables oxidation damping for stable water electrolysis
candidates.authors: Tengyu Chen, Kaiwen Wang, Lu Xia, Wulyu Jiang, Bruna Ferreira Gomes, Linlin Yang, Kaiqi Zhao, Hao Huang, Carlos M. S. Lobo, Ranit Ram, Junmei Chen, Ren He, Alba Garzón Manjón, Kapil Gupta, Zhouhao Zhu, Marinos Dimitropoulos, Viktoria Golovanova, Laís Gimenes Vernasqui, Sven Hörnig, Prathama Haldar, Bárbara Polesso, Aparna M. Das, Sunil Kadam, Andreu Cabot, Jordi Arbiol, F. Pelayo García de Arquer
candidates.abstract: The design of atomically precise catalysts requires strategies that regulate their electronic and structural dynamics under operating conditions. While conventional doping can effectively tune bulk materials, it translates poorly to single-atom catalysts (SACs), in which isolated atoms lack extended coordination and are prone to oxidative instability. Here we design atomically dispersed Ru−O−Cr motifs that enable oxidation damping during acidic oxygen evolution. In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy shows attenuated Ru oxidation synchronized with anticorrelated and partially reversible Cr redox evolution, consistent with proximity-dependent redox coupling. This buffered redox response is accompanied by bounded and partially reversible changes in the local metal−oxygen coordination environment. These coupled dynamics support proximity-coupled Ru−O−Cr redox units, enabling a 55.7-fold increased resistance against oxidation-induced Ru dissolution compared with conventional SACs. In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis, catalysts incorporating proximal Ru−O−Cr configurations exhibit degradation rates that are 6.8-fold and 14.4-fold lower than those of Ru SACs and commercial RuO2, respectively, at 1 A cm−2. These results suggest proximal oxidation damping as a potential design principle for stabilizing atomically precise electrocatalysts. Single-atom catalysts can mitigate reliance on scarce noble metals, but isolated sites can be fragile. Here a catalyst with proximal Ru−O−Cr motifs is fabricated that demonstrates proximal oxidation damping where the Cr neighbour buffers Ru overoxidation, improving stability for acidic oxygen evolution.

candidates.title: Structural basis of ligand-mediated transition to higher-order rubisco assemblies
candidates.authors: Albert K. Liu, Benjamin Kaeser, Jose H. Pereira, Leah J. Taylor-Kearney, Michal Hammel, Eva Nogales, Paul D. Adams, Patrick M. Shih
candidates.abstract: Abstract Proteins often assemble as higher order complexes, underlying a diversity of molecular structures and biological functions. The emergence of protein-protein interactions between binding partners is generally considered to be the primary driver of oligomerization. However, ligand binding has also been demonstrated to affect higher-order assembly, though this phenomenon is not widely considered as a primary driver of oligomerization. Here, we describe the mechanism by which different rubisco oligomeric states are induced via ligand binding. By expanding the phylogenetic sampling of a unique clade of rubisco, we discover a range of oligomeric responses to ligand binding across the phylogeny and identify the structural features responsible for shifts in the oligomeric state that ultimately provide a path to evolving new quaternary structures. Here, we identify a ligand-dependent mechanism giving rise to new protein assemblies, in contrast with the typical process of evolving new protein-protein interfaces directly. Our findings describe a means by which binding and entrenchment of a ligand enables an increase in structural complexity.

candidates.title: Autapse-inspired neuromorphic hardware with synapse–neuron integration for bidirectional feedback control
candidates.authors: Chan Kim, Seonkwon Kim, Jeong Hwan Song, Jongyoung Lee, Leejae Kim, Seongil Im, Hyunsu Ju, Yoon Seok Jung, Gun Hwan Kim, Jeong Ho Cho
candidates.abstract: Abstract Establishing autonomous and energy-efficient feedback control at the hardware level remains challenging because conventional systems rely on centralized processing and continuous external computation, increasing energy consumption and system complexity. Here we show a neuromorphic autapse-inspired system that enables localized and bidirectional feedback control, using thermoregulation as a representative application. An autapse is a self-synaptic connection in which a neuron feeds its output back to its own synaptic input, enabling intrinsic feedback modulation. The system integrates a solid electrolyte-based synaptic transistor capable of multiplexing multiple inputs and a bidirectional leaky integrate-and-fire artificial neuron. By feeding the neuronal output back to an additional synaptic gate, excitatory and inhibitory feedback loops are realized within a compact architecture. Using an artificial thermoregulation platform, temperature-dependent inputs bidirectionally modulate neuronal firing frequency, demonstrating biologically inspired feedback control with a compact set of neuromorphic devices for autonomous and energy-efficient systems.

candidates.title: Phylogeographic and functional assembly of population-level bacterial immunity
candidates.authors: Xuefang Huang, Jingxian Yang, Luokai Wang, Jiayi Zhang, Shuanshuan Xu, Shuangshuang Wang, Xinyan Xu, Luqiong Lv, Pan Tao, Bin Li
candidates.abstract: Bacterial pangenomes provide a shared reservoir of antiphage defenses, yet the ecological and functional constraints shaping this reservoir remain unclear. Here, we combine comparative genomics of 206 Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) genomes with cross-infection assays of 50 strains against 36 phages and heterologous expression of 24 defense systems in a phage-sensitive Xoo chassis. The Xoo pan-defensome comprises a conserved core of 9 subtypes and a variable layer of 35 accessory and cloud subtypes structured by host phylogeography. Phages are more infectious on sympatric than allopatric hosts, consistent with local adaptation. Variable systems show stronger apparent activity than core systems, whereas resistance breadth is not predicted by defense system number. Co-expression of representative co-occurring and mutually exclusive system pairs reveals synergistic and antagonistic interactions underlying non-random repertoire assembly. Together, these findings extend the pan-immunity framework by showing that population-level immune reservoirs are shaped by both ecological structure and functional compatibility. In this study, the authors use comparative genomics and cross-infection assays to show a spatially and evolutionarily structured bacterial immune reservoir in which interactions among defense systems can reinforce or undermine phage resistance, refining the pan-immunity framework.

candidates.title: SIP-enabled multi-omics reveals soil microbiome responses to drought and rehydration
candidates.authors: Tristan A. Caro, Juan Ibarra Arriaga, Grace Solini, Zahra Shivji, Eli Grossman, Aarushi Jhatro, Bryn Stewart, Xiaojing Fu, Alex L. Sessions, Smruthi Karthikeyan
candidates.abstract: Soil microbial activity, and the balance of anabolic (carbon assimilating) and catabolic (CO2-releasing) processes, control the magnitude and direction of soil carbon fluxes. Soil hydration controls this activity, and with hydroclimate volatility increasing across many regions, microbial responses to drought-rewetting cycles urgently require quantification. We conducted rainfall exclusion experiments at two Mediterranean-type field sites, coupling isotope labeling with multi-omics, to link microbial growth, greenhouse gas fluxes, and the carbon sources driving both. Rehydration shortened apparent cell generation times from years to days within minutes. High-intensity drought lengthened the lag before growth resumed, yet metagenomic inference indicated post-drought enrichment of rapid-growth phenotypes. Drought and rehydration shifted the soil metabolome, implicating specific osmolytes in the microbial response and suggesting metabolite diversity modulates microbial function. These results constrain soil microbial activity rates and mechanisms underlying drought-rewetting responses and motivate further study of carbon cycling under increasingly volatile hydroclimates. This study demonstrates that soil microbial growth rates are extremely slow under dry conditions, with rehydration causing a rapid increase in anabolic activity within days. These findings refine our understanding of microbial contributions to soil carbon cycling with a warming climate.

candidates.title: Thin-film lithium niobate waveguide-integrated p-i-n Tungsten selenide photodiodes with 10Gbit/s data reception
candidates.authors: Weijia Tang, Zixian Wei, Ting He, Haoyu Huang, Xin He, Su Wu, Jun Liu, Changyuan Yu, Hongyan Fu, Weida Hu, Shun Wang, Youwei Zhang
candidates.abstract: Abstract Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a promising photonic platform in next-generation integrated optoelectronics and on-chip/chip-chip interconnection due to its attractive optical property and versatility. However, integration of conventional-material-based photodetectors on TFLN platforms still faces multiple challenges. Herein, a high-bandwidth TFLN-based waveguide-integrated lateral WSe 2 p-i-n photodetector is presented. The localized self-aligned doping process eliminates slow carrier diffusion and defect trapping in doped regions which further boosts modulation bandwidth. Secondly, n-type and p-type Ohmic contacts, along with a high-quality p-n junction, are achieved through Se vacancy defect engineering and high-work function molybdenum oxide buffer layer, respectively. Furthermore, combined with the high dielectric constant of lithium niobate suppressing ionized impurity scattering, carrier mobilities exceeding 350 cm 2 /V·s are achieved for both electrons and holes, significantly accelerating carrier drift. The device features a measured bandwidth of 1.12 GHz and a data rate up to 10 Gbit/s in visible light. Separately, the device achieves a responsivity of ~492 mA·W −1 and a near-unity external quantum efficiency of 95.6% at 638 nm. This combination of two-dimensional homostructure and TFLN nano-waveguides provides a basis for high-speed photodetectors and visible-light interconnections in future TFLN integrated optoelectronics and optical input/output applications.

candidates.title: Latitude modulates climate-driven maize yield gains across the central U.S. “warming hole”
candidates.authors: Nenghan Wan, Haidong Zhao, Jerry L. Hatfield, Roger A. Pielke, M. B. Kirkham, Stephen M. Welch, Lina Zhang, Zhijuan Liu, Haishun Yang, Xiaomao Lin
candidates.abstract: Abstract Maize yield responses to climate change differ seasonally and regionally, with both positive and negative impacts shaped by local climate trends and management decisions. Here, using a phenology-aligned moving crop-season framework and the Hybrid-Maize model (1991–2024) across five U.S. Corn Belt states, we quantify climate-driven yield contributions and show that they transition from southern declines to northern gains, reflecting the persistent influence of the central U.S. summer warming hole characterized by cooling maximum temperatures and increasing rainfall. A systematic thermal mismatch between environmental heat availability and hybrid growing degree day requirements is observed, particularly south of 42°N, where thermal matching declined despite favorable thermal conditions. Contrasting trends in thermal matching and reproductive duration help explain the latitude-dependent structure of climate-driven yield contributions. Our findings highlight how hybrid selection modulates the impacts of temperature, precipitation, vapor pressure deficit, and radiation trends on maize yield gains across the U.S. Corn Belt.

candidates.authors: Ryota Aoki, Hidenori Nishihara, Takuya Sakamoto, Yuko Sato, Tae Kuramoto, Makiha Fukuda, Tomoko M. Matsunaga, Ayami Uehara, Daniel Slane, Yuki Kawanishi, Shunnosuke Mori, Daiki Nagaoka, Mayumi Hirakawa, Hengbin Gao, Daiki Maejima, Yuki Minoura, Yumiko Suto, Kotaro Ishii, Colin J. candidates.abstract: Horizontal gene transfer drives rapid evolutionary innovation, yet well-substantiated cases are largely confined to prokaryotes. Eukaryote-to-eukaryote transfer remains exceptionally rare, and direct genome-scale demonstrations are absent. Here, inspired by endosymbiotic genome acquisition, we show that mammalian cells can initiate genome-scale horizontal gene transfer through phagocytic uptake of intact algal cells, albeit at a much lower frequency than cell fusion. Live-cell imaging captures the early nuclear appearance of transferred algal DNA after fusion, while genome sequencing and cytogenetic analyses reveal stable retention of chromosome-scale algal DNA in mammalian cells. Hybrid cells maintain more than 16 Mb of algal DNA, including intact chromosomes, as telomere-linked structures that persist for 95 generations without selection. Transferred algal DNA shows a progressive increase in DNA methylation together with enrichment of repressive histone modifications, forming heterochromatic domains that physically associate with host chromosomes. Notably, mammalian cells deficient in a de novo DNA methyltransferase show reduced stable establishment and retention of transferred algal DNA, supporting a gatekeeping role for DNA methylation in the stable accommodation of foreign genomes. Our findings reveal an epigenetic mechanism that contributes to the stable accommodation of large-scale foreign DNA between distantly related eukaryotes. Aoki et al. show that mammalian cells can acquire and retain chromosome-scale DNA from algae. The study reveals that host DNA methylation helps establish and maintain foreign DNA, offering insight into gene transfer between distant species.

candidates.title: Extinction risks in deep-sea populations revealed by genomic data and ecological niche modeling
candidates.authors: Pedro A. Peres, Keith Sellers, Tracey T. Sutton, Heather Bracken-Grissom
candidates.abstract: As the global biodiversity crisis accelerates across terrestrial and shallow marine systems, the extent of this collapse remains unknown within the deep sea. Despite encompassing most of the ocean, deep-sea ecosystems remain the planet’s final frontier. Within this vast realm, the mesopelagic zone represents a critical yet poorly understood habitat, particularly in terms of its conservation status. Here, we integrate genomic data with ecological niche modeling to assess and forecast the conservation status of five mesopelagic species in the Gulf of Mexico. Samples were collected from 2011 to 2023, representing one of the longest time-series datasets for mesopelagic fauna in oceanographic history. All species exhibit current effective population sizes below the minimum thresholds for long-term viability. Genomic diversity declined over a decade in some species at rates comparable to or exceeding those reported for threatened and endangered species. Demographic modeling indicates historical population declines across all species. Ecological niche models predict declining Gulf habitat suitability for most species under future climate change scenarios. Together, our results identify indicators associated with elevated extinction risk in Gulf mesopelagic species and raise the possibility of a broader, unnoticed crisis, challenging assumptions of stability and resilience in mesopelagic ecosystems. Here authors use genomic data to reveal indicators of elevated extinction risk in Gulf of Mexico mesopelagic species. Together with projected declines in habitat suitability, these findings raise the possibility of a broader, unnoticed crisis.

candidates.title: Cobalt based anode for highly stable alkaline water electrolysis under operation conditions beyond industrial requirements
candidates.authors: Jinchao Zhu, Tianyu Qiu, Sixie Zhang, Cheng Han, Wenwen Xu, Suyang Feng, Haocheng Chen, Yingjie Wen, Xinlong Tian, Sheng Dai, Zhiyi Lu
candidates.abstract: Alkaline water electrolysis is the most established route to electrochemical hydrogen production, but the limited lifetime of anode catalysts makes long-term equipment investment costly and hinders miniaturization. Here we show that, unlike the extensively investigated nickel- and nickel–iron-based hydroxides, the long-neglected cobalt–nickel hydroxides are promising anode catalysts whose stability exceeds current industrial requirements. A cobalt–nickel layered double hydroxide anode enables stable alkaline water electrolysis for more than 8,000 hours at 1 A cm–2 in 6 M sodium hydroxide at 80 °C. This stability arises from the strengthened metal–oxygen bonding of the in-situ-formed cobalt–nickel oxyhydroxide, which raises the energy barrier for lattice-oxygen loss during the oxygen evolution reaction. In a practical electrolyzer, the anode achieves an energy consumption of ~4.2 kWh per normal cubic metre of hydrogen at 1 A cm–2 and operates stably for thousands of hours. The design of high-current-density alkaline electrolyzers should therefore prioritize robust anode stability under industrial conditions in addition to activity optimization. Hydrogen production by alkaline water electrolysis is limited by anode durability under industrial conditions. Here, the authors demonstrate a cobalt–nickel layered double hydroxide anode that sustains operation for over 8,000 h at 1 A cm⁻² in 6 M NaOH at 80 °C, enabling durable hydrogen production.

candidates.title: Scaling medical imaging report generation with multimodal reinforcement learning
candidates.authors: Qianchu Liu, Sheng Zhang, Guanghui Qin, Yu Gu, Ying Jin, Sam Preston, Yanbo Xu, Sid Kiblawi, Wen-wai Yim, Timothy Ossowski, Tristan Naumann, Mu Wei, Hoifung Poon
candidates.abstract: Abstract In medical imaging report generation, supervised fine-tuning can overfit to superficial patterns and generalize poorly across institutions. We introduce Universal Report Generation (UNIRG), which adopts reinforcement learning to directly optimize clinically meaningful quality criteria. With this framework, we developed UNIRG-CXR, an 8-billion-parameter vision–language model trained on four public datasets (MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert Plus, ReXGradient-160k and IU-Xray) by supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning (group-relative policy optimization) against a composite lexical, semantic and clinical-error reward. We evaluated held-out test sets and an external proprietary dataset, with RadCliQ as primary metric and expert radiologist validation. Here we show that our method improves report quality and generalization: UNIRG-CXR surpasses prior models on the ReXrank benchmark across four datasets and two generation settings, exceeding the previous best score by over 50% on two test sets, and produces fewer clinically significant errors while maintaining performance on unseen data sources and across demographic subgroups.

candidates.title: A prefrontal microcircuit computes trial-wise discount of reinforcement during threat learning in male mice
candidates.authors: Xin Yi, Ming-Yang Wei, Tong-Zhou Yu, Wenying Xu, Yan-Jiao Wu, Qi Wang, Xue Gu, Yong-Ling Wang, Hoiyin Cheung, Ting-Ting Zhang, Qing-Ren Cao, Yuan-Bo Zhang, Hai-Ling Li, Lu-Yang Wang, Peng Yuan, Tian-Le Xu, Wei-Guang Li
candidates.abstract: Threat learning requires rapid adaptation, but how the brain weights successive aversive experiences remains unclear. Here we show that many male mice exhibit delayed freezing acquisition during auditory fear conditioning. A trial-wise discount reinforcement learning model captured these dynamics through transient attenuation of early associative updating. Medial prefrontal neurons projecting to the periaqueductal gray constrained acquisition and subsequent cue-evoked freezing: inhibition increased freezing, whereas activation reduced it. Calcium imaging of individual neurons identified a subpopulation with delayed post-shock responses that declined during learning and predicted the model-derived discount-like variable. Temporally restricted inhibition implicated activity extending beyond the shock in constraining early acquisition. Local somatostatin interneurons showed increasing shock-evoked activity and provided inhibitory input to these projection neurons, suggesting a mechanism for relaxing this constraint. These findings link the trial-wise weighting of aversive experience to a prefrontal inhibitory microcircuit and provide a framework for understanding individual differences in threat memory formation. Neural mechanisms underlying threat learning are not fully understood. Here authors identify a prefrontal circuit that constrains early threat learning in male mice. Local inhibitory neurons may release this constraint, providing a mechanism for regulating how strongly each experience shapes memory.

candidates.abstract: Biological nitrogen (N2) fixation is crucial for incorporating atmospheric N2 into the biosphere. However, its evolutionary trajectory remains enigmatic, particularly given the presumed scarcity of molybdenum (Mo) in Archean seawater prior to oxidative weathering and the apparent early emergence of Mo-based nitrogenase over its vanadium (V)-based alternatives. Here, we integrate partitioning experiments with an extensive analysis of iron-rich sediments through time to investigate the behavior of Mo and V in ancient seawater. Our results suggest that, during the Archean to Paleoproterozoic, dissolved V was removed from seawater more efficiently than Mo, primarily through preferential incorporation into banded iron formations (BIF). Consequently, Mo was likely more available in seawater than commonly assumed, with Archean seawater characterized by higher Mo/V ratios than today. Greater Mo availability relative to V provides a compelling explanation for the earlier evolution of Mo-based nitrogenase despite the absence of widespread oxidative weathering, and helps resolve the apparent paradox surrounding the early evolution of biological N2 fixation. Partitioning experiments and Fe-rich sediments show V was removed from Archean– Paleoproterozoic seawater more efficiently than Mo, enriching seawater in Mo relative to V and helping explain the early evolution of Mo-based nitrogenase.

candidates.title: ISG15 promotes PARP inhibitor resistance in BRCA1-deficient cells by facilitating DNA replication and repair
candidates.authors: Rebecca A. Dagg, Teressa Paulsen, Birbal Prasad, Giuliana De Gregoriis, Yuri Seung, Florian J. Groelly, Simeon D. Draganov, Flaminia Pedretti, Andrea Herencia-Ropero, Violeta Serra, Adán Pinto-Fernández, Madalena Tarsounas
candidates.abstract: Abstract The use of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) has proven largely successful in targeting BRCA1/2 -mutated tumours. However, the emergence of PARPi-resistant disease can reduce the efficacy of this treatment, posing significant challenges in the clinic. Here, we use multiple models of BRCA1 -/- cells and patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) that have been treated with PARPi until they no longer responded to the drug, to characterise genomic and transcriptomic alterations specific to PARPi resistance. We find that abrogation of TP53BP1 expression occurs spontaneously during prolonged PARPi treatment, alongside TP53BP1 genomic deletions and promoter methylation. Additionally, innate immune response genes, including ISG15 and factors of the ISGylation machinery are upregulated in PARPi-resistant cells and tumours. We demonstrate that ISG15 inhibition re-sensitises PARPi-resistant cells to the drug and, conversely, that ISG15 overexpression in BRCA1 -/- cells promotes PARPi resistance. Mechanistically, BRCA1 -/- PARPi-resistant cells rely on ISG15 for replication fork progression and restart of stalled forks and for DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair via homologous recombination (HR). Our results indicate that complex ISG15 interactions with DNA replication/repair factors can drive PARPi resistance in BRCA1-deficient cancer cells and that targeting ISG15 has the potential to overcome PARPi resistance.

candidates.authors: Leonard Leong, Mansi Narula, Johannes Englisch, Cheryl Ou, Maksim Mamonkin, Norihiro Watanabe
candidates.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-modified Vδ2 T cells are an attractive therapeutic cell platform for cancer immunotherapy. However, their clinical efficacy is limited by short in vivo persistence due to insufficient cytokine support and high susceptibility to activation-induced cell death (AICD). Through comparison of membrane-bound (mb) cytokines, we identified mbIL-18 to support superior anti-tumor activity of CAR-Vδ2 T cells in vitro and in vivo. To reduce constitutive surface exposure of IL-18 and enable antigen-driven signal 3, we fused MyD88 - the key IL-18R signaling mediator - to an extracellular domain of Fas (Fas88). Antigen stimulation-induced FasL engagement of Fas88 triggered IL-18 signaling while simultaneously protecting Vδ2 T cells from AICD. Fas88-armed human CAR-Vδ2 T cells produced superior yet stimulation-dependent in vivo expansion and functional persistence in xenograft models of hematologic and solid malignancies. Together, these findings highlight the importance of IL-18 signaling and AICD resistance for CAR-Vδ2 T cell activity, enabling a single-transgene modification to limit inflammatory risk and facilitate clinical translation. CAR-Vδ2 T cells show promise for cancer immunotherapy, but their efficacy is limited by poor persistence and activation induced cell death. Here, this group propose an engineered CAR-Vδ2 T design that leverages IL18 signaling inducing a durable expansion in vivo.

candidates.title: Emergent stoichiometric host-guest recognition on ligated colloidal surfaces via dynamic ligand reorientation
candidates.authors: Wenya Li, Zhucheng Yang, Vikas Tiwari, Jia Liu, Yirong Wang, Yilin Xie, Huitao Huang, Ruoyang Chen, Junyu Ke, Shijin Lin, Tarak Karmakar, Shun-Li Li, Ya-Qian Lan, Jianping Xie, Yitao Cao
candidates.abstract: Physical adsorption on ligand-protected colloidal nanoparticles is central to their properties and applications, yet adsorption events on dynamic ligand shells are rarely defined, counted, or quantified with molecular precision. Here we show that on a native ligand shell without pre-designed receptor-like motifs, molecular adsorption can trigger stoichiometric host-guest recognition through dynamic ligand reorientation. In aqueous dispersion, atomically precise [Au25(p-MBA)18]− (p-MBA = para-mercaptobenzoic acid) nanoclusters accommodate tetraalkylammonium ions within transient aromatic pockets formed by three to four neighboring p-MBA ligands. NMR titration and diffusion-ordered spectroscopy reveal an apparent saturated binding number of six guests per nanocluster, with an apparent association constant of ~3.5 × 104 M−1 and ΔG of ~−25 kJ•mol−1 for tetrapropylammonium binding. Molecular simulations and free-energy analysis rationalize this stoichiometry through a cooperative yet self-limiting mechanism, in which ligand reorientation creates bowl-like pockets stabilized by multiple CH···π interactions while steric constraints limit further guest accommodation. The guest-size- and surface-dependent binding behaviors further reveal the adaptive nature of emergent pockets. These findings change the role of the ligand shell from a stabilizing layer or diffuse adsorption medium to an active supramolecular interface capable of producing molecularly defined recognition, paving the way for adaptive nanomaterials, selective sensing, and stimuli-responsive colloidal systems. Here the authors show that molecular adsorption can trigger stoichiometric host-guest recognition through dynamic ligand reorientation.

candidates.title: Constructing exclusive Pt@WOx interfacial sites enables selective C–O bond activation
candidates.authors: Jieqi Zou, Dawei Zhou, Qian He, Binbin Zhao, Chao Zhu, Lei Liu, Jinxiang Dong
candidates.abstract: Precisely constructing exclusive metal-oxide interfacial active sites while eliminating non-interfacial species represents a longstanding challenge in heterogeneous catalysis. Here we construct catalysts featuring exclusively isolated Pt@WOx interfacial sites via a controlled electrostatic adsorption strategy, thereby eliminating non-interfacial Pt species, enabling controlled reaction pathways. We identify that selective C–O bond activation is governed by the availability of interfacial reactive hydrogen, where isolated Pt sites drive deep hydrogenolysis, while Pt@WOx interfacial sites control reaction pathways by constrained hydrogen availability. This principle is validated in glycerol hydrogenolysis, achieving a high 1,3-PDO selectivity of 73.5% at a low temperature of 130 °C. Experiments reveal that 1,3-PDO selectivity is not enhanced by increasing active site density, but by eliminating intrinsically unselective sites, thereby reshaping the reaction energy landscape to suppress thermodynamically driven over-hydrogenolysis. This architecture provides an ideal platform for disentangling interface effects from contributions arising from non-interfacial metal species. Precisely constructing metal–oxide catalysts with exclusively interfacial active sites remains challenging. Here, glycerol is selectively converted to 1,3-propanediol over catalysts in which Pt exists solely as isolated Pt@WOx interfacial sites.

AGO1 is the major effector of microRNA (miRNA) and 21/22-nucleotide (nt) secondary small interfering RNA (siRNA) pathways in Arabidopsis thaliana. Here, we validate a functional nuclear localization signal (NLS) in the N-terminal extension of AGO1 and identify IMPORTIN α2 (IMPα2) as a nuclear import factor acting within a larger importin α network. Using engineered nuclear-only and cytoplasmic-only AGO1 variants, we show that exclusive cytoplasmic AGO1 allows full miRNA target repression and secondary siRNA production in ago1 mutants, whereas nuclear-retained AGO1 only partially rescues miRNA function and exerts a dominant-negative effect on secondary siRNA biogenesis. sRNA immunoprecipitation assay reveals that miRNAs are preferentially loaded into AGO1 in the nucleus, while tasiRNA loading predominantly occurs in the cytoplasm. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that AGO1 spatial partitioning itself quantitatively shapes the efficiency and specificity of sRNA loading and the silencing outputs. Small RNAs guide ARGONAUTE proteins to their targets. candidates.title: scMomer: a pretraining framework for inferring robust cellular representations from single-cell transcriptomes
candidates.authors: Yuhang Liu, Quan Zou, Ran Su, Leyi Wei
candidates.abstract: High-quality cellular representations are important for understanding complex biological systems. However, due to limitations in both data availability and practical utility, most existing computational methods are designed for a single modality (e.g., scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq), restricting their ability to capture cellular heterogeneity. Here, we propose scMomer, a multistage pretraining framework designed to infer robust cellular representations by integrating multimodal knowledge into scRNA-seq-only inputs. The framework progressively learns through three stages. Firstly, it pretrains unimodal encoders on single-modality datasets to obtain modality-specific representations. Secondly, it aligns these modalities using paired data to learn joint representations. Thirdly, it applies knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge of the missing modality (scATAC-seq) into a cross-modal student encoder, enabling the inference of multimodal-aware representations from scRNA-seq-only inputs. We perform extensive experiments show that the representations learned by scMomer achieve superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods across diverse tasks, including cross-modality translation, cell annotation, drug response prediction, perturbation prediction, and gene property prediction, demonstrating its robustness and versatility. Overall, we demonstrate that scMomer enables unimodal data to yield robust cellular representations, providing an effective solution to missing-modality modeling. Here, the authors develop scMomer, a pretraining framework that infers multimodal-aware cellular representations from scRNA-seq data alone. By distilling chromatin accessibility knowledge, the authors show that this method can be applied to different downstream single-cell tasks.

candidates.authors: Andrea Cataldo, Emil J. Bergholtz, Daniel Leykam, Jun Gao, Ali W. Elshaari
candidates.abstract: Topology under non-Hermitian dynamics is encoded in the phase of the bulk evolution, yet strong dissipation suppresses the amplitudes carrying it. We resolve this using a programmable photonic integrated circuit that implements such dynamics in synthetic momentum space through unitary dilation, with the phase recovered by phase-shifted interferometry. For the non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, the method distinguishes trivial and nontrivial Zak phases and yields a coherence winding q = ± 1 induced by an exceptional point. Extending to a synthetic torus via a Rice-Mele pump gives the first Chern number Ch 1 = 0 , 1 for trivial and nontrivial cycles, showing a programmable route to momentum-space topology under strongly dissipative non-Hermitian dynamics.

candidates.title: Unveiling High-Energy Ultrafast Responses Driven by Fermi-Level Gap Opening in Charge-Density Waves
candidates.authors: Qiong Wu, Tianchen Hu, Junhan Huang, Yongjie Liu, Fei Sun, Shuxiang Xu, Li Yue, Zijian Lin, Xinyu Zhou, Tao Dong, Nan-Lin Wang
candidates.abstract: Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy is indispensable for investigating interactions, collective excitations, and nonequilibrium dynamics in superconductors and correlated electron systems. However, how a small gap opening near Fermi surface affects the spectral changes in the high-energy interband transition region remains elusive. To address this issue, we perform systematic studies of carrier relaxation dynamics in the prototype charge-density-wave (CDW) material EuAl4. We find that the CDW gap shrinks substantially under optical pumping. This band renormalization strongly modulates interband transitions associated with the gap edge, inducing a pronounced transient reflectivity change at the corresponding probe energies. These results establish a direct link between low-energy order-parameter dynamics and high-energy spectral responses, providing a general framework for interpreting transient signals in gapped quantum materials.

candidates.title: Hilbert Space Fragmentation from Generalized Symmetries
candidates.authors: Thea Budde, Marina Kristć Marinković, Joao C. Pinto Barros
candidates.abstract: Hilbert space fragmentation refers to exponential growth in the number of dynamically disconnected Krylov sectors with system size. It is taken as evidence of ergodicity breaking, since conventional symmetries generate at most a polynomial number of sectors. However, we demonstrate that generalized symmetries, including higher-form, subsystem, and gauge symmetries, can have exponentially many symmetry sectors in the tensor product basis. We further prove that noninvertible symmetries can induce additional fragmentation within individual symmetry sectors. Fragmentation in several known models arises from generalized symmetries, and the presence of exponentially many Krylov sectors therefore does not by itself imply ergodicity breaking. Finally, we show that disorder free localization arises from Krylov-restricted thermalization when sectors lack translation invariance, requiring neither ergodicity breaking nor gauge symmetry.

candidates.title: Quantum Theory of Exciton Magnetic Moment: Interaction and Quantum Geometric Effects
candidates.authors: Gurjyot Sethi, Jiawei Ruan, Fang Zhang, Weichen Tang, Chen Hu, Mit Naik, Steven G. Louie
candidates.abstract: Combining magnetometry with optical spectroscopy has uncovered novel quantum phenomena and is emerging as a powerful probe of quantum materials. However, the theory of the magnetic response of excitons, correlated electron-hole pairs in insulators, remains incomplete due to insufficient treatment of electron-hole interactions and quantum geometric effects. In biased bilayer graphene, for instance, theoretical predictions of valley g-factors for p-excitons deviate from experiment by nearly an order of magnitude. Here, we develop a quantum theory of the exciton orbital magnetic moment, based on first-order perturbation theory within the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter Equation approach and a rigorous treatment of the position operator in the response of exciton states to a magnetic field. Our formalism reveals three distinct contributions that go beyond the heuristic approaches used in the literature: a Berry-phase-corrected single-particle electron and hole moment difference, a term from envelope-function winding linked to electron-hole relative motion, and a center-of-mass correction from exciton band quantum geometry, with the latter two being completely new effects not considered in previous studies. Our ab initio calculations yield results in excellent agreement with experiment, establishing the importance of interaction and quantum geometric effects in the magnetic response of excitons.

candidates.title: Is the Large Uncertainty of δ C P Fundamentally Encoded in the Neutrino Quantum State?
candidates.authors: Michela Ignoti, Claudia Frugiuele, Matteo G. A. Paris, Marco G. Genoni
candidates.abstract: The precise measurement of the leptonic -violating phase δ C P remains one of the major open challenges in neutrino physics, as current experiments achieve only very limited accuracy. We address this issue through the lens of quantum estimation theory. A distinctive feature of neutrino oscillation experiments is that they cannot freely optimize the probe or measurement, since both are constrained by the production and detection of flavor eigenstates. We therefore examine whether the large uncertainty in δ C P originates from intrinsic properties—either of the neutrino quantum state or of flavor measurements—or if it instead stems from experimental limitations. By comparing quantum and classical Fisher information, we demonstrate that the limited sensitivity to δ C P originates primarily from the information content of flavor measurements. Furthermore, we show that, while targeting the second oscillation maximum, as in the ESS ν SB proposal, typically enhances δ C P information, this feature in fact strongly depends on the actual values of δ C P .

candidates.title: Spontaneous Oscillations and Geometric Cutoff in Confined Bacterial Swarms
candidates.authors: Bing Miao, Lei-Han Tang
candidates.abstract: Self-organized dynamic patterns in dense active matter are striking manifestations of non-equilibrium physics. A prominent example is the macroscopic elliptical motion observed in quasi-2D bacterial suspensions, which has lacked a physical explanation. Here, we examine a minimal linear response framework coupling bacterial swimming dynamics with fluid flow, treating long-range hydrodynamic interactions as a macroscopic communication channel. We demonstrate that microscopic swim motion, via Jeffery coupling, manifests as a ``phase-leading'' response to local shear flows. System-wide sustained oscillations, on the other hand, require both a critical bacterial density and strict geometric confinement. By analytically predicting the onset cell density and maximum film thickness, our model achieves excellent quantitative agreement with experiments, establishing a unified physical framework for self-organized periodic motion of elongated body in active fluids.

candidates.title: Interpreting Liouvillian Eigenmodes: Quantized Orbits in Dissipative Systems
candidates.authors: Ashlin V. Thomas, Felix Fritzsch, Masudul Haque, Shovan Dutta
candidates.abstract: In closed quantum dynamics, energy eigenstates represent physical excitations which, for systems with a classical limit, localize on quantized orbits in phase space. Such a picture is lacking in open systems: Liouvillians have distinct right and left eigenstates that decay with time and are difficult to interpret. We recover a physical correspondence by introducing a gauge-invariant quasiprobability measure combining right and left eigenstates that interprets a Liouvillian mode as a set of coherences, allowing one to visualize the modes as quasiprobability distributions in a “doubled” phase space. Using this measure we show that, remarkably, a damped oscillator retains its quantized “orbits” for a large class of linear and nonlinear loss, with measurable signatures. A thermal bath broadens these orbits, similar to energy levels, leading to a characteristic multistage relaxation. This provides an experimentally accessible open-system analog of the eigenstate-orbit correspondence underlying semiclassical quantization. For quadratic systems, our results yield dissipative analogs of invariant tori—a central concept in Hamiltonian systems.

candidates.title: Landscape of Scattering Universality with General Dispersion Relations
candidates.authors: Yidan Wang, Xuesen Na, Michael J. Gullans, Susanne F. Yelin, Alexey V. Gorshkov
candidates.abstract: Universality in physics describes how disparate systems can exhibit identical low-energy behavior. Here, we reveal a rich landscape of new universal scattering phenomena governed by the interplay between an interaction and a system's density of states. We investigate one-dimensional scattering with dispersion relations $ε(k)=|k|^m$ and $ε(k)=\operatorname{sgn}(k)|k|^m$ for any real $m>1$. For emitter scattering and separable potentials, including contact potentials, we classify the zero-energy $S$-matrix limits. These universal $S$-matrix fixed points depend solely on the dispersion exponent $m$ and a finite set of integers characterizing the low-momentum interaction structure. This classification extends far beyond the standard quadratic-dispersion case ($m=2$). We further derive a generalized Levinson's theorem relating the total winding of the $S$-matrix determinant to the number of bound states. Finally, for contact potentials and analytic monomial dispersions, we analyze the leading low-energy expansion of the scattering phase near these fixed points and extract the corresponding Wigner-delay scaling. Our findings are directly relevant to synthetic quantum systems, where engineered dispersion relations in atomic arrays and photonic crystals offer a platform to explore these universal behaviors.

candidates.title: Excitonic-Superconducting Coexistence and Emergent Nematic Superconductivity Driven by Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
candidates.authors: Fei Yang, Ruigang Li, Junwei Liu, Binghai Yan
candidates.abstract: Excitonic insulating (EI) and superconducting (SC) orders are generally regarded as mutually exclusive electronic instabilities. Within a self-consistent microscopic theory, we study electronic systems hosting an EI phase in the presence of SC pairing and show that an intrinsic mismatch between electron and hole Fermi surfaces fundamentally reshapes this competition. This mismatch stabilizes FFLO-like electron-hole pairing and drives spontaneous symmetry breaking of the EI state. The resulting symmetry breaking reconstructs the pairing phase space for SC and EI state, such that different regions of the Fermi surface complementarily support either EI or SC correlations, leading to a natural coexistence of the two orders. Notably, the emergent SC state consequently breaks rotational symmetry and develops intrinsic nematic superconductivity, even in the absence of explicit symmetry-breaking fields (such as magnetic fields, spin-orbit coupling, or bare band-structure anisotropy). Our results suggest that candidate materials such as monolayer 1T$'$-MoTe$_2$ and the square-net semimetal NaAlSi may provide promising platforms for observing this phenomenon. More broadly, these findings reveal a unique mechanism by which competing many-body orders generate electronic nematicity, suggesting a broader route toward spontaneous anisotropic electronic states in correlated quantum materials.

candidates.title: Realization of a Cavity-Coupled Rydberg Array
candidates.authors: Jacopo De Santis, Balázs Dura-Kovács, Mehmet Öncü, Adrien Bouscal, Dimitrios Vasileiadis, Johannes Zeiher
candidates.abstract: Scalable quantum computers and quantum networks require the combination of quantum processing nodes with efficient light-matter interfaces to distribute quantum information in local or long-distance quantum networks. Neutral-atom arrays have both been coupled to Rydberg states to enable high-fidelity quantum gates in universal processing architectures, and to optical cavities to realize interfaces to photons. However, combining these two capabilities and coupling atom arrays to highly excited Rydberg states in the mode of an optical cavity has been an outstanding challenge. Here we present a novel cavity-coupled Rydberg array that achieves this long-standing goal. We prepare, detect, and control individual atoms in a scalable optical tweezer array, couple them strongly to the optical mode of a high-finesse optical cavity and excite them in a controlled way to Rydberg states. We show that high-cooperativity coupling to an optical cavity—demonstrated via the dispersive shift of the resonance of the cavity in presence of the atoms—and strong Rydberg interactions—demonstrated via the collective enhancement of Rydberg coupling in the atomic array—can be achieved in our setup at the same spatial location. Our presented experimental platform opens the path to several new directions, including the realization of quantum network nodes, quantum simulation of long-range interacting, open quantum systems, and photonic-state engineering leveraging high-fidelity Rydberg control.

candidates.abstract: Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ is a Mn-based kagome metal that has been proposed to be close to a ferromagnetic instability. Recent $^{55}$Mn nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) study suggested the emergence of a spin-singlet paired state below $\sim$10 K. To clarify its low-energy magnetic and electronic properties, we performed $^{55}$Mn NMR and nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR) measurements on single-crystalline Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$. From the detailed NMR/NQR spectrum measurements and the DFT calculations, a quadrupolar frequency of $ν_{\rm Q}$ = 4.6$\sim$4.8 MHz and an asymmetry parameter of $η$ = 0.45$\sim$0.48 as well as the principal axes of electric field gradient EFG for the Mn site were determined. The temperature dependence of Knight shift ($K$) shows a similar temperature dependence of the DC magnetic susceptibility $χ$ except for the low-temperature region below $\sim$ 50 K where $K$ is almost constant while $χ$ keeps increasing, which suggests that the increase in $χ$ at low temperatures is not intrinsic. $^{55}$Mn spin-lattice relaxation rate divided by temperature ($1/T_1T$) is found to be nearly constant, confirming the metallic state of Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ from a microscopic point of view. Furthermore, no peak in $1/T_1T$ is observed near 10 K, and neither the Knight shift nor the linewidth shows any reductions at low temperatures. These results suggest no clear signature for the spin-singlet pairing around 10 K in Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$.

candidates.abstract: $α$-In$_2$Se$_3$ is a two-dimensional van der Waals material with promising applications involving ferroelectricity. However, the presence of native defects can significantly influence its structural and electronic properties. In this work, we employ density functional theory with a state-of-the-art meta-generalized gradient approximation (meta-GGA) exchange-correlation functional to investigate the electronic structure of bulk $α$-In$_2$Se$_3$ and the formation of neutral point defects, including vacancies and antisites, under Se-rich and In-rich growth conditions. Our calculations reproduce the experimental structural parameters of the pristine material and reveal that the Se vacancy in the middle layer exhibits an unexpectedly low formation energy under both chemical environments. Structural analysis shows that the neighboring tetrahedrally coordinated In atom undergoes a substantial local relaxation along the three-fold axis, which preserves its $C_{3v}$ site symmetry even as its coordination is reduced from four to three, providing a microscopic explanation for the remarkable stability of this defect.

candidates.abstract: Competition between spin and valley orders makes graphene a versatile platform for engineering correlated topological phases in the quantum Hall regime. We show that a tunable superlattice potential reorganizes this competition, and stabilizes the ferromagnetic quantum Hall topological insulator at charge neutrality without requiring a large in-plane magnetic field or strong dielectric suppression of Coulomb interactions. The interaction anisotropies responsible for choosing between different competing states are first computed by a generalized renormalization group procedure that accounts for the superlattice potential. We find that the potential suppresses anisotropies that compete with spin-polarization. At the same time, the potential introduces dispersion which prefers a partly spin-polarized compensated semi-metal. Therefore, we carry out a self-consistent momentum-space Hartree-Fock computation with renormalized aniostropies to establish the regime of stability of the insulating spin-polarized ferromagnet. Finally, we verify that this ferromagnet is adiabatically connected to the quantum Hall ferromagnet, thereby confirming its topological character. Our results establish superlattice potentials as a means of controlling the phase diagram of interacting graphene and accessing its helical quantum Hall regime.

candidates.abstract: Motivated by superconductors discovered in systems with a strong Coulomb repulsion, we ask whether such a repulsion can give rise to superconductivity with a transition temperature $T_c$ bounded only by the electron bandwidth. Coulomb repulsion can produce pairing as it binds electrons to holes. If each hole binds three electrons into a three-electron-one-hole (3e1h) composite, the condensation of these bosonic composites can give rise to superconductivity. However, the resulting $T_c$ falls far below the electron bandwidth in the controlled regime where the binding is much stronger than the carriers' kinetic energy. This is because, on a lattice, a tightly bound composite usually has to move through a higher-order process where the intermediate state costs an energy of order the binding energy, so that the strong binding makes the composite heavy, limiting the superfluid stiffness and hence $T_c$. Here, we show that symmetry offers a way around this tradeoff. In lattices satisfying certain symmetry requirements, a composite can move by single-particle hops without any costly intermediate state, a motion we call rolling. Such rolling keeps the mass of the composite finite even for an infinitely strong binding, so that a $T_c$ proportional to the electron bandwidth can be achieved in the controlled regime. We derive a criterion for rolling and apply it to construct all fourteen minimal lattice models that support such rolling. We show that rollable 3e1h composites can indeed be stabilized in the ground state. We then propose to realize such superconductivity in a dual-gate bilayer, and use exact numerics to show that $T_c$ can reach a few percent of the electron hopping. These results establish rollability as a guiding principle in the search for and design of superconductors in strongly repelling electron systems, with the minimal models constructed here as prototypes.

candidates.abstract: We prove a volume-uniform Gaussian approximation for local spin coordinates in the zero-field nearest-neighbour $O(N)$ model on periodic boxes of side $M$ in $d\ge3$, at and below the critical temperature of the limiting spherical model. On a fixed spatial window, for sufficiently large $M,N$, the unnormalized $1$-Wasserstein error for the first $p\le N$ coordinates is at most $C\sqrt p (N^{-1/2}+s_M)$, where $s_M\to0$ is the spectral shift of the finite-volume mean spherical model. The estimate is uniform on compact ranges of positive directional couplings and inverse temperatures. The target has independent coordinate fields, each a scaled anisotropic Gaussian free field with an independent spatially constant Gaussian term below criticality. On a window containing a nearest-neighbour star (a site and its $d$ positive-direction neighbours), the error tends to zero as $M,N\to\infty$ exactly when $p=o(N)$ and $\sqrt p s_M\to0$. candidates.abstract: Conventional descriptions of collective ordering often assume spatially uniform order parameters, although the underlying electronic states can exhibit strong spatial inhomogeneity or multifractality. Here, we demonstrate that deterministic aperiodic geometry can instead stabilize multifractal collective order. We formulate a general diagnostic applicable to superconducting, magnetic, and charge channels, combining direct scaling analysis of the order parameter with three criteria: its spatial hierarchy must be dictated by the underlying geometry, emerge in the leading ordering instability, and persist in the self-consistent ordered state below a single mean-field ordering onset. We demonstrate that superconductivity on the experimentally resolved Ti network of a dodecagonal oxide quasicrystal satisfies all three criteria. The resulting condensate exhibits multifractal scaling over the resolved range of spatial scales, retaining its hierarchical structure throughout the ordered phase and channeling flux-induced equilibrium currents along geometry-locked rings.

candidates.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of mortality worldwide, highlighting the need for rapid, sensitive and reliable detection of cardiac injury at the point of care. Here, we develop a dual-sensor platform that combines an aptamer-functionalized molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) field-effect transistor (2D-FET) with a graphene-based ion-sensitive field-effect transistor (ISFET) for the detection of cardiac troponin I (Trop-I) in complex biological matrices. The atomically thin MoS2 channel enables highly sensitive detection of Trop-I, achieving a limit of detection of 0.001 ng mL-1. However, the high ionic strength of serum substantially attenuates the field-effect response, resulting in approximately 80% degradation of the sensor response. To address this matrix effect, the ISFET is employed as a secondary sensor to characterize the ionic environment of the sample. Machine-learning-assisted integration of the 2D-FET and ISFET responses is investigated as a strategy for compensating serum-induced signal distortion and recovering key electrical figures of merit extracted from the 2D-FET transfer characteristics, including maximum on-state current (Ids_max), subthreshold slope (SS) and transconductance (gm). This dual-sensor architecture combines molecular recognition, high analytical sensitivity and matrix-aware electrical signal correction, providing a potential pathway towards more reliable FET-based biomarker detection in complex biological fluids. The approach may further enable multiplexed detection of cardiac biomarkers through incorporation of target-specific aptamers, offering potential for broader assessment of cardiac stress and myocardial injury risk.

candidates.abstract: Magnetic domain walls (DWs) are central to emerging spintronic technologies for memory, logic and neuromorphic computing, where their controlled displacement is a key functionality. While current-induced DW motion driven by spin-orbit torques is well established under direct currents, it remains unclear how radio-frequency (RF) currents couple to DWs and whether they can generate directed motion under a symmetric periodic drive. Here we show that RF currents drive DW oscillations, which can be rectified into directed motion through symmetry breaking. Using time-resolved and static magneto-optical Kerr microscopy, we demonstrate that RF spin-orbit torques efficiently excite low-frequency DW oscillations well below the ferromagnetic resonance frequency. Whereas these oscillations remain symmetric in the absence of perturbations, symmetry breaking by a transverse magnetic field produces self-propulsion, while symmetry breaking by an initial current pulse gives rise to sustained DW motion. We further show that in initially uniform magnetic states, RF-driven expansion of a pulse-generated edge domain ultimately results in efficient RF-assisted magnetic switching. Together, these results establish a general framework for understanding how RF-driven DW oscillations are rectified into directed motion, providing new opportunities for their high-frequency control.

candidates.abstract: The antiferromagnetic Ising chain in transverse and longitudinal fields exhibits a continuous critical point, a mixed-order transition line and, with quenched disorder, an infinite-disorder fixed point and reentrant order. Using exact free-fermion solutions and the density-matrix renormalization group, we examine what the zeroth persistent homology of staggered ground-state correlations adds to conventional responses. Its barcode records the merge scales of the single-linkage hierarchy, and the maximum of its persistence-landscape velocity defines a threshold-free pseudocritical point. This point locates the clean critical point and the mixed-order line with an accuracy comparable to conventional responses. In the reentrant regime, the global velocity misplaces the entry, which is recovered only by restricting the filtration to the ordering scale, and none of the tested estimators locates the exit. A domain wall forced by the boundary conditions suppresses the disorder-averaged reentrant lobe. For individual disordered realizations, the labelled merge tree recovers most strong-disorder renormalization-group clusters, including noncontiguous ones missed by lattice-restricted hierarchies, with increasing agreement at stronger disorder. This information resides in the full correlation matrix, while zeroth homology provides a stable, threshold-free hierarchy.

candidates.abstract: Despite their promise, the targeted synthesis of novel MXenes remains challenging due to their vast structural and compositional space and the lack of reliable stability descriptors that account for synthesis conditions. To address this gap, we utilized density functional theory (DFT) with the r$^2$SCAN functional to develop a high-fidelity dataset of 1,040 ordered binary and ternary bare delaminated MXenes, including mono-transition metal MXenes, in-plane ordered double-transition metal MXenes, in-plane ordered metal-divacancy MXenes, and out-of-plane ordered double-transition-metal MXenes. For each structure, we calculated formation and decomposition Gibbs energies, decomposition products, layer symmetry groups, and energies above the hull. We find that all MXenes are thermodynamically inaccessible under equilibrium conditions. However, 115 predominantly carbide MXenes become thermodynamically stabilized at elevated temperatures (500--2000 K), and 23 are stabilized under high pressure (10 GPa). Additionally, three MXenes in the Mn--Fe--C chemical space are stabilized within an experimentally feasible range of carbon chemical potentials. These findings reveal stability trends across the MXene space and identify synthesis strategies that can guide experimental efforts. Our dataset provides a robust foundation for developing machine-learned stability descriptors and for guiding experimental efforts toward novel MXene discovery. By identifying synthesizable candidates along with their synthesis conditions, this work bridges a critical gap in data-driven approaches to MXene discovery and lays the foundation for future autonomous experimental workflows.

candidates.abstract: Motivated by recent proposals of $p$-wave magnets, which host odd-parity spin splitting, we study electrons near Van Hove singularities with local repulsive interactions. We demonstrate how the symmetry of the $p$-wave spin splitting governs the competition among instabilities. Using a parquet renormalization group (pRG) analysis of a simple one-sublattice model of a $p$-wave magnet, we find that superconductivity is the leading instability over the entire phase diagram for purely repulsive interactions. The resulting superconducting state is generically a mixture of spin-singlet and spin-triplet pairing and approaches an equal-weight mixture when $T_c$ is small compared with the energy offset between each Van Hove electron and its inversion partner. Extending the pRG analysis to a more realistic two-sublattice model, we find that superconductivity remains the leading instability, while the sublattice degree of freedom leads to a competition among various singlet-triplet pairing channels and even a finite-momentum equal-spin pair-density wave. Our mechanism applies broadly to odd-parity magnets and opens a natural route to nodal topological superconductivity.

candidates.abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are prime nanofluidic conduits and nanopores for studying matter under extreme confinement. Since most synthesis routes yield CNTs with closed ends, opening and filling strategies are required to access their interior for fluid and ion transport, whereas studies of the encapsulated species themselves may additionally require sealing to prevent their escape in dry or vacuum environments. Capacitively coupled local anodic oxidation (LAO) in an atomic force microscope (AFM) has been shown to cut individual CNTs at predefined positions, but whether cutting induces opening, filling, or sealing has remained unclear. Using spatially resolved micro-Raman spectroscopy, we find that LAO cutting surprisingly produces filled CNT segments that remain sealed under dry Ar atmosphere for weeks. The magnitudes of the blueshift and broadening of the innermost-wall radial breathing-like mode are consistent with water filling, pointing to the water meniscus condensed between the AFM tip and the substrate as the source of CNT filling during cutting. High-vacuum annealing at 140 °C releases the encapsulated species from some, but not all, segments, indicating a thermally surmountable barrier rather than re-formed end caps. This one-step cut-fill-seal capability offers a route to diameter-resolved studies of nanoconfined water and aqueous solutions, and to zeptoliter-scale sample delivery for vacuum-based analytical techniques.

candidates.abstract: We use density functional theory to map the lattice-dynamical landscape of BaSnO3 under biaxial compressive strain and uncover the hierarchy of structural instabilities. Our results demonstrate that the phase stability of strained BaSnO3 cannot be inferred from the softening of the polar mode alone. Instead it is governed by the competition among lattice instabilities and their anharmonic coupling to structural relaxation. Two-mode energy-surface analyses show that the polar and rotational order parameters interact predominantly competitively. While A- and M-point octahedral rotations become unstable before the zone-center polar mode and dominate the harmonic response for moderate values of strain, they are related to a continuous transition without anharmonic lattice coupling and a moderate gain of energy with strain. Large strain may induce a first order transition to a supertetragonal polar state. Once this state is stabilized, the magnitude of polarization and ferroelectric energy well depth are comparable to BaTiO3 under compressive strain. Furthermore, we discuss how an electric field or electron doping may tip the balance between the different modes and favor of the supertetragonal structure over antipolar and rotational alternatives at a reduced critical strain.

candidates.abstract: Passive probes in active baths can undergo spontaneous motion driven by nonequilibrium forces that depend on probe velocity and interaction geometry. Using trajectory-response relations that express the bath response to a probe in terms of free-particle displacement statistics, we investigate the dynamics of freely moving probes weakly coupled to ideal active baths. The mean force exerted by the bath defines a velocity-space potential whose minima describe the stable states. By analyzing how the mean force depends on the probe velocity, we identify stable resting and moving states and determine the parameter regime in which they coexist. For elliptical interactions, the resting state becomes unstable first along the narrow axis, resulting in direction selection already at the linear-response level. For fourfold interactions, linear friction remains isotropic, while the nonlinear dependence of the mean force on probe velocity selects axial or diagonal motion and produces directional multistability. We further show that the trajectory-response relations extend to higher orders in the probe strength, where multi-interval free-particle trajectory statistics become relevant. For a Gaussian probe, these higher-order terms shift the speed of the stable moving state.

candidates.abstract: The central limit theorem is among the most fundamental principles in the natural sciences, governing the fluctuations of sums of weakly correlated random variables through Gaussian statistics. At critical points, however, long-range correlations invalidate this paradigm, raising a fundamental question: does any general limit theorem survive at criticality? Although scale invariance has long been recognised as the defining feature of typical critical fluctuations, the behaviour of rare fluctuations has remained largely unexplored, as their extraordinarily small probabilities place them beyond the reach of conventional numerical methods. Recent theoretical advances suggest that universal asymptotic laws {may govern large deviations in systems at criticality}, yet direct numerical evidence has been lacking. Here we provide the first such evidence in the two-dimensional Ising universality class. Using large-scale Tethered Monte Carlo simulations, we probe order-parameter fluctuations with probabilities as small as $10^{-200}$ and show that, once normalised by their characteristic width, the far tails collapse onto a single asymptotic law shared by distinct microscopic models in the same universality class. candidates.abstract: Layered magnetic materials with tunable valley and spin degrees of freedom hold promise for multifunctional spintronic devices. Here, we demonstrate that the orientation of an in-plane electric field enables selective switching of single-valley spin splitting and reversal of the anomalous Hall conductivity in strained bilayer MoO. In particular, electric fields along the a and b directions selectively lift the spin degeneracy at the X and Y valleys, respectively, while preserving it at the other valley. This valley-selective switching is accompanied by a redistribution of Berry curvature with opposite signs, giving rise to a reversible anomalous Hall response. These effects are realized in the energetically and dynamically stable AC2 stacking configuration, where biaxial strain induces Dirac-like band crossings that enable subsequent electric-field control. Meanwhile, the AC1 stacking configuration, which is also energetically and dynamically stable, exhibits rich strain-driven phenomena, including a transition from metal to topological insulator with quantized spin Hall conductivity, as well as valley polarization and piezomagnetism. Our findings reveal a combined effect of strain and electric fields for controlling valley-selective spin splitting and anomalous Hall responses, highlighting bilayer MoO as a promising platform for multifunctional spintronic and valleytronic devices.

candidates.abstract: Chiral molecules adsorbed on a magnetic film interact with its magnetization and can thereby alter the thermal motion of magnetic skyrmions. Here we develop a theoretical model in which an aligned layer of tilted molecules modifies the interfacial magnetic interactions according to its handedness. Within this model a skyrmion responds only to spatial variations of the coupling, so a uniform layer leaves its position unaffected, whereas boundaries and coverage gradients exert forces on it. Near a chiral region, these forces deflect the skyrmion transversely in a direction that reverses between enantiomers, which provides a direct signature of the chiral interaction. In extended periodic patterns, the same forces reshape the long-time diffusion, suppressing it in the direction in which the potential varies and enhancing it in the perpendicular direction. The net effect on the mean diffusion is set by the balance between the gyrotropic and dissipative responses of the skyrmion, as we show exactly for one-dimensional landscapes. Stochastic micromagnetic simulations and collective-coordinate calculations confirm these predictions and show how molecular orientation, spatial patterning, and skyrmion properties together determine the motion.

The composition-temperature phase diagram reproduces the known transition sequences and temperatures of both end members and reveals an intermediate tetragonal $I4/mcm$ phase near the boundary that has no counterpart in either parent compound. Above the transition temperatures the $B$ cations remain locally off-centered but orientationally disordered. The structural transition at the boundary causes a jump in the band gap at low temperature, whereas at $350$ K the gap decreases smoothly with Sn content. These results establish $B$-site mixing as a means to tune polar and rotational order in lead-free halide perovskites.

candidates.abstract: A boundary can release spin-polarized electronic states from a magnetically compensated, spin-degenerate layer. We establish the symmetry criterion governing this release in coplanar exchange magnets: the allowed even-parity edge-spin space equals the allowed uniform-magnetization space. Symmetry-protected compensation therefore selects an odd spin texture perpendicular to the moment plane. Six maximal sectors organize the possible edge textures. Orthogonal cuts of one exchange model realize odd and even sectors, while FeSe spin-vortex and NiI$_2$ period-four spiral Wannier models provide material realizations. Their semi-infinite boundaries exhibit complementary electrical responses: perpendicular spin accumulation at the odd edge and in-plane spin-current response at the even edge. Boundary symmetry thus connects magnetic compensation to equilibrium spin textures and electrical spin readout.

candidates.abstract: Negative thermal expansion (NTE) in framework materials arises from complex lattice dynamics that are challenging to capture using conventional theoretical approaches. Here, we establish a hierarchical computational strategy for investigating NTE in ZrV2O7, integrating the quasiharmonic approximation (QHA), temperature-dependent effective potentials (TDEP), and machine-learning-accelerated ab initio molecular dynamics (ML-MD). Quasi-harmonic lattice-dynamical calculations identify low-frequency phonon modes with negative Grüneisen parameters as inexpensive screening descriptors, while TDEP incorporates finite-temperature anharmonicity and ML-MD further reveals temperature-dependent structural distortions that drive the lattice contraction. The observations are further corroborated with X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements. The concurrent increase in transverse displacement (uT) provides microscopic evidence for a quasi-rigid-unit-mode (QRUM) mechanism underlying the NTE behaviour at elevated temperatures. This is consistent with previous reports on other framework materials, including ZrW2O7, where collective polyhedral rotations and transverse atomic motions have been linked to NTE. Overall, our results demonstrate how relatively inexpensive lattice-dynamical descriptors can identify potential NTE materials, while higher-level anharmonic simulations can then resolve the underlying structural mechanisms at the atomic scale.

candidates.abstract: We study the long-time statistics of spatial moments of the time-dependent energy distribution in a one-dimensional Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti model following an instantaneous release of energy on a single lattice site. The moments are $M_n(T)=\sum_i x_i^n u_i(T)$, where $u_i(T)$ is the energy at site $i$ at the observation time $T$. Employing macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT), we calculate the variance of $M_n$ for every positive integer $n$ and determine the non-Gaussian distribution tails for the representative cases $n=1$ and $2$. For the first moment, we establish an exact duality, within MFT, to integrated-current statistics for a deterministic flat initial density. For both $n=1$ and $n=2$, the large-moment tails are dominated by a single adiabatically evolving doublon: a rapidly propagating pair of narrow solitary pulses of the energy density and of the gradient of the conjugate field. The small-second-moment tail is associated with concentration of the energy near the origin at time $T$. Comparing single- and two-doublon histories, we predict a dynamical phase transition at a critical value of $M_2$ at which the optimal path breaks reflection symmetry $x\to -x$. candidates.abstract: Optically addressable electron spins are promising platforms for quantum technologies, with molecular systems offering chemical control over their spin and optical properties. Achieving optical readout of molecular spin states at room temperature and without an applied magnetic field is an important step towards their practical implementation. Quintet states generated via singlet fission are promising optically addressable multilevel qudits, but their intrinsic spin transitions at zero and weak magnetic fields remain largely unexplored, while substantial room-temperature quintet coherence has predominantly been demonstrated in structurally constrained molecular architectures. Here, we combine zero-field optically detected magnetic resonance (zero-field ODMR) with transient and pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) to investigate the magnetic-field dependence and coherent spin properties of quintet states in conformationally flexible, through-space coupled tetracene oligomers. We demonstrate zero-field optical readout of quintet states at room temperature in both tetracene dimers and hexamers, and map the response of optically detected transitions to weak applied magnetic fields. Complementary EPR measurements support quintet formation through stochastic exchange fluctuations and demonstrate a room-temperature phase-memory time of 446 ns, showing that the conformational dynamics enabling high-spin formation remain compatible with substantial spin coherence. Together, these results integrate field-free optical readout, weak-field response and room-temperature spin coherence within a chemically modular, through-space coupled molecular architecture, expanding the design space for optically addressable molecular qudits and quantum sensors.

candidates.abstract: Chalcogenide alloys such as the prototypical Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ compound are used in phase change electronic memories due to their ability to undergo a fast and reversible transition between the amorphous and crystalline phases upon heating. The amorphous phase is subject to aging that leads to an increase in the electrical resistance, which is detrimental to the operation of the devices. Using a machine learning interatomic potential, we have investigated the structural relaxations responsible for aging in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ in molecular dynamics simulations at temperatures slightly below the glass transition. The aging simulation, lasting about 100 ns, follows an equilibration of 24 ns at 400 K. During aging we observed an enhancement of the Peierls distortion in axial bonds which is a typical feature of these alloys that we relate to the widening of the electronic band gap computed within Density Functional Theory in smaller aged amorphous models. We also observed a marked reduction of the atomic mobility with an increase of the bond lifetimes during aging. However, we do not see a reduction in homopolar bonds, which are expected to be absent in the ideal aged glass and which should be removed on a much longer time scale.

candidates.abstract: The influence of defect topology and chemical doping on the optical response of amorphous silicon (a-Si) remains unresolved. In this study, hybrid-functional density functional theory and linear-response calculations are employed to examine four structurally distinct continuous random networks with substitutional boron and phosphorus doping. The calculated optical properties reproduce key experimental trends and demonstrate that dopant sensitivity is determined not only by defect concentration, but also by the character and spatial organization of defects. A configuration with fully extended 4-fold coordination shows the strongest dielectric perturbation to doping, while dopant effects in networks with pre-existing defect states are more varied. For most networks, the dielectric response is more strongly perturbed by boron than phosphorus. Notably, a network having both 3- and 5-fold defects with a total defect fraction of 7.4% reverses the typical boron-dominant response of other cases, becoming more sensitive to phosphorus. Tauc and optical sum-rule analyses further indicate that network topology defines the broader optical landscape, whereas doping primarily affects states near the gap and redistributes spectral weight. These findings establish defect topology as a microscopic control parameter that links amorphous structure, dopant activity, and optical response in amorphous silicon.
